rationale: M60 XML ONTOLOGY CENSUS, verdict GAP for `extends`, implemented. The census found `extends` at ZERO edges on a corpus where XSD writes the relation in the vocabulary's own name: XSD 1.0 Part 1 s3.4.2 XML Representation of ComplexType Definitions defines both `<extension base = xs:QName>` and `<restriction base = xs:QName>`, and the attribute is documented as the qualified name of the BASE TYPE. The mechanism is called type DERIVATION throughout Part 1, and both alternatives produce a subtype: extension keeps everything the base admits and adds to it, restriction narrows the content model to a subset. `extends` is the ontology's name for exactly that relation, so both emit `extends` rather than the `references` this lane gave every `base=` value — the same relabel as the `calls` finding, and for the same reason, that an edge can be real and carry the neighbouring type. The lane's own written ruling said otherwise — 'A complexType is not a subclass of another, it REFERENCES one by base — and publishing that as extends would be a category error' (script/m14/spec/xml-completeness.json, notApplicable) — and the measurement is what settled it: the construct the ruling assumed absent is written by the specification, and the corpus carries it in every schema language family present (89 of the corpus's XSD files write xs:extension, 89 write xs:restriction, across dbeaver, otp, phpunit, powershell, grails-core). Three derivations are pinned here because they take three different paths, and the third is the one that keeps the edge honest. (1) IN-DOCUMENT: `Derived` extends `Base`, declared at line 10 of this file, so the target symbol is published and the edge resolves at both ends. (2) BUILT-IN: `Code` restricts `xs:token`, so the edge is emitted carrying `resolvable: builtin` and — the assertion that matters — NO `token` symbol is published, because a built-in is not a declaration in this file and inventing one is the M60.R10 lie the reference pass already refuses. (3) UNSATISFIED: `FromElsewhere` extends `tns:Absent`, a name this document declares nowhere and imports from nowhere. The reference pass refuses exactly this shape for a prefixed value (the `xml/xsd-external-reference` fixture), and so does the derivation pass: the edge is not emitted, because per-file analysis cannot tell a missing declaration from one an `xs:include` brings in. Two things are pinned in metadata rather than left to the reader. `derivation` says which of the two it is, because a consumer asking 'what does Code extend' needs to know the answer narrows rather than widens. And `resolvable` says whether the base could be found at all, so a builtin subtype never reads as an in-document one. The source of each edge is the anonymous `xs:extension`/`xs:restriction` element rather than the derived type's name, which is this analyzer's pre-existing convention for an inline construct with no declared name. Reaching the type actually being derived walks the containment chain back up, and the two derivations differ in depth — `Derived -> xs:complexContent -> xs:extension` is two hops, `Code -> xs:restriction` is one — so both are pinned. That convention is recorded as a declared limitation rather than quietly left to be discovered.

expectSymbols.name: xs:extension
expectSymbols.note: the inline derivation element IS published, as its tag, because it has no declared name of its own. It is the source of the extends edges and the target of `contains Derived -> xs:extension`, so the edge resolves at both ends without a second convention for anonymous declarations.

expectRelationships.note: SOURCE CORRECTED 2026-10-04, and this is the substantive change in this fixture's history. This edge used to be asserted with `from: "xs:restriction"`, which is the XSD vocabulary's own word for a type CONSTRUCTOR and not a type at all. The analyzer computed an attribute's owner as the element the attribute sits on (src/ast/real-xml-analyzer.ts, `symbolName = declaredName ?? name`), and an inline `<xs:restriction>` carries no `name`, so the owner fell back to the tag text. Measured over the full 11,456-file admitted corpus that put a fabricated source on **438 of 438 `extends` edges — 100%, with zero sources a document declares** (validation/m14/fixtures/xml/derivation-accounting.mts). `extends` relates two TYPES, so its source must be the nearest ancestor that DECLARES a name. The analyzer now threads that ancestor (`nearestNamedSchemaOwner`) and the fabricated count is 0 of 1,429. The note that previously called the old source "an anonymous inline element" and argued the real type was reachable via `bb_graph` owner-cascade was a rationalisation: owner-cascade attributes MEMBER rows to an owner class, and `xs:restriction` is not a member of `Version` in that sense.

the ownership hop that names the derived type. It is TWO hops to `Derived` — `Derived -> xs:complexContent -> xs:extension` — not one, and this assertion was written expecting one and failed, which is why it is here in this exact form: the extends edge's source is an anonymous inline element, and reaching the type that is actually being derived walks the containment chain back up. `bb_graph`'s owner-cascade attributes member rows to the owner class, so the answer is reachable without a second convention for anonymous declarations. Present before the relabel and still present after it — extends is added beside contains, not in place of it.

the same hop for the restriction case, and here it IS one hop because `<xs:simpleType>` has no `complexContent` wrapper. The two derivations differ in depth, which is why the fixture pins both rather than one representative shape.

forbidRelationships.note: the negative half of the relabel. An XSD derivation is `extends` (s3.4.2) and must not ALSO be a `references` edge; edge identity is source|type|target, so emitting both would put one fact under two labels and make 'does this type extend Base or merely mention it' unanswerable.
same negative half for the restriction case, which is the one a copied rule would leave behind: a rule that diverts `xs:extension` and forgets `xs:restriction` keeps this edge as a reference.

the refusal under test. `tns:Absent` is declared nowhere in this file and imported from nowhere, and from inside this file an `xs:include` could still be what supplies it — the identical ambiguity the reference pass records for bare values and refuses for prefixed ones (pinned by xml/xsd-external-reference). Publishing the edge would put a name in the graph that no file supports.

the written value is not a name: the target of a derivation is the LOCAL NAME, and the prefix rides in metadata (M60.R10, a value where a name belongs). No declaration in this file carries a colon-bearing name.

`type=` is a reference and stays one. s3.4.2 defines `base` as the base TYPE; `type` names the type an element's VALUE has, which is a different relation, and relabelling it would be inventing a supertype where the document states a value type.

THE REGRESSION PIN for the fabricated-source defect, kept as a forbid because the wrong edge is the one that must never come back. `xs:restriction` is a schema CONSTRUCTOR, not a declared type: the document declares `Version` and declares nothing called `xs:restriction`. An `extends` edge whose source is a vocabulary tag is a name in the graph that no file supports, which is what makes a fake caller into wrong refactoring advice in bb_graph, bb_impact and bb_migrate. This row is the same pair the fixture's own expectation used to carry.

forbidSymbols.name: token
forbidSymbols.note: XSD declares `token` in Part 2, not in this file. The extends edge to it is emitted with resolvable: builtin; publishing a symbol would be a phantom declaration of a name this document never declares — the M60.R10 class, and the reference pass's existing refusal.

forbidSymbols.name: Absent
forbidSymbols.note: the unsatisfied base: no declaration, so no symbol. Same reasoning as the edge it would have hung on.

forbidSymbols.name: tns:Base
forbidSymbols.note: the written value, not the local name a declaration carries.

_targetSpelling: THE SAME-FILE TIER (2026-10-12): a target this file declares under EXACTLY ONE owner is emitted as `Owner.name` — the two-part identity the analyzer already computes (`qualifiedName = ownerName + '.' + name`) and which `parallel-indexer.ts:3435-3437` already looks up — so the store binds it without a store change. The bare name stays in `metadata.bareTarget`. A target the file declares under ZERO or 2+ owners is left exactly as it was.
